Olomi clinched the title with a total of 229 strokes, 13 over par, finishing five shots ahead of Ghana’s Afi Amez edo, who returned 234 strokes to claim second position.
The Tanzanian opened with a two-over-par 74 in the first round, followed with a 75 in the second round before carding 80 in the final round to secure the overall victory.
Tanzania’s Olomi Takes Early Lead As 100 Golfers Battle For Nigeria Ladies Open Title
Speaking after her triumph, Olomi attributed her success to hard work and her determination to excel, describing the victory in Nigeria as another indication of progress in her golfing career.
Tanzania also dominated the leading positions, with Madina Hussein finishing third on 238 strokes, 22 over par, after rounds of 76, 83 and 79.
Her compatriot Hawa Wanyeche placed fourth with 241 strokes, while Loveness Mungure and Aalaa Somji returned identical totals of 254.
Ghana’s Wendy Gyan and Zimbabwe’s Tracey Humbira also finished level on 256 strokes.
Nigeria’s best performers were Omowonuola Olarewaju, who returned 271 strokes, and Josephine Benjamin, who finished with 274. Susan Marcus and Dorcas Daniel recorded 276 and 279 strokes respectively.
The championship was organised by the Ladies Golf Association of Nigeria (LGAN) and attracted female golfers from several African countries.
LGAN President, Dr Lami Onayi Ahmed, commended the participants for their sportsmanship, saying the competition had contributed to strengthening relationships among African countries through golf.
The closing ceremony featured presentations of trophies and golf bags to sponsors, distinguished personalities, spectators, LGAN executives and members of the Local Organising Committee.
Among those recognised was Kayode Adeniyi, General Manager of NTA Sports, who served as Director of Communications for both the All Africa Challenge Trophy and the 2026 Nigeria Ladies Open.
